newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end down on Brazil worries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end down on Brazil worries.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly lower Wednesday as worries over allegations of bribery in the Brazilian government prevented the market from benefitting from market friendly U.S. producer price figures.

"The market is partially affected by Brazil," said a trader. In addition, after the recent run up the market may have reached a cap until the outcome of the May 20 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve is known, said the trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at 92-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.15 at 115.10.
"Until everything is defined," on the U.S. monetary policy front, the market could tread water, added the trader.

However, another trader said Wednesday's U.S. producer price figures showing a decline of 0.6 percent in April made it more likely the Federal Reserve will only hike rates once Just one more hike in the year should be absorbed relatively easily by the market, allowing Argentine bonds to gain more in coming months, players said.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.53 percent from 6.48 percent.
